title: Read the Exception Queue
scenario: It is 1:00 PM - exception-working time. Today the queue is empty: INV-58831 sailed through auto-approve. But an empty queue is a result, not an accident. Learn what the exception queue is for, what lands here, and why 'nothing to work today' is exactly what a healthy clean day looks like.
input: Exception queue: 0 items. The match decision routed the only invoice we followed (INV-58831) to auto-approve. Anything the decision cannot clear - price outside tolerance, quantity mismatch, a suspected duplicate, or a vendor not in the master - would land here for a human on the AP desk to resolve before it can be paid.
instructions: Read the exception queue as the human-review path off the match decision's fork.
Answer the four questions about what lands here and why today's queue is empty.
Validate to mint the exception-resolution record (an empty, clean-day record).

questions.prompt: What kind of invoice lands in the exception queue?

options.text: Every invoice, for a second review
Any the match decision could not clear - out of tolerance, quantity mismatch, duplicate, or unknown vendor

questions.explain: The queue is the other branch of the fork. It catches exactly the invoices that failed a check, so a human resolves them instead of the system paying blind.

questions.prompt: Why is the queue empty today?

options.text: INV-58831 passed every check and was auto-approved, so nothing needed a human
Exceptions are ignored on clean days

questions.explain: An empty queue is a healthy result: the day's invoice was clean on tolerance, quantity, and duplication, so it never branched to human review.

options.text: A human on the AP desk (Clerk, escalating to the AP Manager)

questions.explain: Exceptions exist precisely because a machine could not decide. The AP Clerk investigates and the AP Manager approves any resolution before the invoice can rejoin the payment path.

questions.prompt: Why still produce a record when the queue is empty?

options.text: To prove the queue was checked and nothing was outstanding at cutoff
There is no reason to record an empty queue

questions.explain: An explicit 'zero exceptions, checked at 1:00 PM' record proves the desk did not simply forget to look. Absence of work is documented, not assumed.

artifactOnPass.sources: match-decision failures (tolerance, quantity, duplicate, unknown vendor)
artifactOnPass.workedBy: AP Clerk, approved by AP Manager

successMessage: Exception queue read. Zero items today - a clean day, documented rather than assumed.

intro.heading: Before you batch: the other path

sections.title: The fork's second branch
sections.body: The match decision sends clean invoices to auto-approve and everything else here. The exception queue is the human-review path - the safety valve for anything a machine should not decide.

sections.title: What lands here
sections.body: Price outside tolerance, a quantity mismatch, a suspected duplicate, or a vendor not in the master. Each is a case where paying automatically would be a mistake, so a person steps in.

sections.title: Empty is a healthy result
sections.body: Today INV-58831 passed every check, so the queue is empty. That is not luck to gloss over - it is the clean-day outcome the whole pipeline is designed to produce.

sections.title: Document the absence
sections.body: Even zero exceptions gets a record: checked at 1:00 PM, nothing outstanding. Proving the desk looked and found nothing is different from never having looked.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd drop mismatched invoices into a review queue (a shared list or ticket) with a note on what failed, for a human to resolve.

bestFit.how: a review app over the exceptions table, so the queue is worked where it lives
a 'Create Record' into the exceptions table plus a channel message naming the assignee

takeaway.heading: Exception queue read
points: You answered the four questions: what lands here, why the queue is empty, who works it, and why absence is still recorded.
The queue is the fork's human-review branch - it catches exactly what the match decision could not clear.
Today it is empty because INV-58831 passed every check, which is the healthy clean-day outcome.
An explicit zero-exceptions record proves the desk checked, rather than assuming nothing was there.
The workflow can now route unclear invoices to a human while proving the clean ones needed none.
